newsitem.title: USA: Campbell Soup may shed noncore lines - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Campbell Soup may shed noncore lines - WSJ.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co is considering shedding "nonstrategic" businesses with $1.4 billion is sales, in a move to focus on volume growth in its core soup, sauces, biscuits and food service lines, The Wall Street Journal said.
In Monday's electronic edition, the paper said Campbell executives told securities analysts that no decisions had been made on the form of the potential divestitures.

Though the company did not disclose which brands it is considering getting out of, businesses that are not in the company's core areas include Swanson frozen foods, Vlasic pickles, fresh mushrooms sold under the Campbell brand and some small international operations, the article said.
The Journal quoted one analyst as saying the businesses could potentially be worth about $750 million, if sold.
